issues.item: Checking Surroundings: constantly scan environment for signs of threat
issues.explanation: The profile is not well aligned with the cognitive formulation. The only active edge is Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies, so maladaptive strategies should plausibly arise from the selected appraisals. Overeating and busyness can follow from distressing appraisals, but 'Checking Surroundings' is a threat-monitoring/safety behavior that usually implies an active Threat component or a strong Trigger/Threat linkage, both of which are absent in the formulation and not represented elsewhere in the self-report.

issues.item: Fear of Harm: You can never know who will harm you
issues.explanation: 'Fear of Harm' is a global current-danger appraisal that typically pairs with a Threat presentation and supports behaviors like environmental scanning. But Threat is not represented as an active component in the formulation, and the rest of the negative appraisals are more about self-doubt and shattered assumptions. This makes the appraisal/strategy pattern clinically incoherent for the specified edge structure.

vignette: John, a 77-year-old married man and long-time delivery driver, has been struggling with the aftermath of an assault that occurred several months ago. The traumatic event was sudden and vicious: while making his rounds on a quiet evening street, he was ambushed by a masked assailant who attacked him without warning. John had come to believe that such violence would never happen in his neighborhood or during one of his routine deliveries. This unexpected attack shattered his sense of security and control over his environment. Since the assault, John has been plagued by intense feelings of self-doubt and confusion about how he should respond to everyday situations. He often finds himself questioning whether he will do the right thing, particularly when faced with choices that might put him in a vulnerable position again. This constant uncertainty leads him to work excessively hard at keeping busy with other tasks to distract himself from these intrusive thoughts. John had come to believe that if he thinks about the event too much, he will not be able to handle it. This belief has led him to suppress his thoughts and memories of the assault through various maladaptive strategies. One such strategy is overeating; John often finds himself reaching for food as a way to manage his distress. The more he indulges in eating excessively, the less control he feels he has over his life, which only reinforces his self-doubt. The trauma has also affected his work as a delivery driver. John’s occupation requires him to navigate unfamiliar and sometimes isolated areas, making it challenging for him to avoid places that trigger flashbacks or feelings of vulnerability. He tries to keep himself busy with deliveries to avoid thinking about the assault, but this busyness often leaves him exhausted and further distracts from his emotional well-being. John’s marriage has also been impacted by these struggles. His wife notices changes in John’s behavior and is concerned about how he isolates himself when they are at home. Despite her support, John feels like he cannot fully trust that he will do the right thing to keep their family safe or to handle his own emotions effectively. The incident has left John with a sense of shattered beliefs about the world around him. He no longer trusts that his environment is safe and secure, which makes it difficult for him to engage in activities outside of work without feeling anxious. This anxiety further fuels his overeating and excessive busyness as ways to cope with his internal turmoil. John’s most recent encounter with these overwhelming emotions occurred when he was driving past the street where the assault took place. The trigger brought back vivid memories, leading to a surge of distress that he tried to suppress through increased eating and working longer hours than usual. This cycle has left him feeling physically drained and emotionally exhausted. It is this constant state of emotional strain and his growing sense that he cannot manage his thoughts and feelings effectively that finally pushed John to seek help. He hopes to regain control over his life and find healthier ways to cope with the trauma without relying on maladaptive strategies like overeating or busyness. What frightens him most is the fear of being unable to protect himself and his loved ones, but he remains hopeful for a future where these fears no longer dominate his daily existence.
